key_insight: WebHarbor packages 153 reconstructed websites into executable, Docker-based environments for GUI agents. It aims to combine the realism of live websites with the stability needed for repeatable evaluation and training.
problem_solved: Live websites change over time, restrict access, and make authenticated workflows difficult to evaluate. Synthetic alternatives often lack realistic visuals and functional depth.
method: Reconstruct website interfaces, content, and functionality to support realistic GUI interaction.
Package 153 executable website environments in Docker for controlled deployment.
Use these environments as stable settings for GUI-agent evaluation and training.
impact: WebHarbor could help practitioners test and train web agents without relying on unpredictable live websites. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no quantitative performance results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: changing live websites versus controlled Docker-based replicas.
Pipeline diagram: website reconstruction → Docker container → GUI-agent interaction.
A grid of website windows labeled “153 executable environments.”
Icons highlighting realism, stability, and interactive functionality.
paper_title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
paper_authors: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou, Demi Wang, Jiacheng Zhang
